basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 13.' and it opens '(Vers. 13.) Et qui fugerat, nuntiavit Abram transitori. Ipse vero sedebat ad quercum'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 13.) Et qui fugerat, nuntiavit Abram transitori. Ipse vero sedebat ad quercum Mambre Amorrhaei fratris Eschol, et fratris Aunam, qui erant conjurati Abrahae. Pro eo, quod nos posuimus, transitori, in Hebraeo scriptum est IBRI (עברי), hoc enim transitor exprimitur. Quod autem ait: apud quercum Mambre Amorrhaei, melius in Hebraeo legimus, apud quercum Mambre Amorrhaei fratris Escol: et fratris, non Aunam, ut Septuaginta transtulerunt, sed Aner: ut ostenderet Mambre et Escol, et Aner Amorrhaeos atque germanos, socios fuisse Abrahae.
